deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 34% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.0% = 10-year Treasury 5.0% + 5%; base: sales × its 3-year median free-cash margin (3%), because current free cash flow is negative). note.headline: Amazon rises 3.47% to 255.39 amid reported AI deal; still waiting for 238.65

summary.thesis: Amazon's margins are improving, but it is burning cash and its sales growth is slowing, and at 255.39 the price is already in the upper half of its own fair-value range.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: no trade, because the price sits in the middle of a range with resistance just above it.

note.happening: The stock rose 3.47% to 255.39. That put it back near its 50-day average of 255.07 and inside a price zone of 251.93–258.08. Several outlets reported that Amazon is buying the AI start-up Decart for $7.5bn, to gain its chip-software technology as Amazon prepares to sell its Trainium chips. Amazon has not confirmed the deal in a filing. There is no earnings date in the data, and one headline reported that the Nasdaq is 'in freefall'.
note.business: The things that change the business point in two directions. Margins are improving: operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. Cash is the problem. Free cash flow (cash left after spending on the business) over the last 12 months was -46.9B, down from +10.6B a year earlier. Net debt is 66.7B (net cash of -66.7B). Demand is cooling: quarterly sales growth was 12.09%, down from 16.61% two quarters ago. Unpaid customer bills rose 61% while sales rose 12%. That can mean sales are being pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. The reported Decart deal is about competition in AI chips (general knowledge: it supports the cloud business). At the reported price it adds to cash spending, but it does not change this quarter's demand. The worker dispute over data centres and the New York City shipping-label complaint matter for sentiment and regulation, not for current results. What is not at risk: liquidity of 114.2B covers near-term needs. What is at risk: the stock's valuation if growth keeps slowing while spending stays high.

worth.text: No discounted-cash-flow value is possible because free cash flow is negative. So the only fair-value method is Amazon's own price-to-sales history (price divided by sales per share): 187.93 at the low end, 238.65 in the middle and 265.96 at the high end. At 255.39 the price is above the middle and below the top. Amazon's price-to-sales of 3.5 sits at the 62nd percentile of its own 5-year history. That is far below the peer median of 6.0, and 0.63 of the peers on a growth-adjusted basis. The gap between 'cheap versus peers' and 'fully priced versus its own history' depends on which yardstick applies. Earnings multiples look moderate: 20.7 times trailing earnings and 20.0 times this year's. But analysts expect next-year earnings of 10.67 per share, below 12.8 this year, so the multiple rises to 23.9. The filings flag that the price implies about 34% yearly growth, against 13% a year delivered over 3 years. Note: the valuation summary in the data was computed at 246.82, before today's rise.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.0.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales is producing more profit.
Price-to-sales of 3.5 is well below the peer median of 6.0, and only 0.63 of peers on a growth-adjusted basis.
Revenue over the last 12 months reached 797.5B, up from 691.3B, and the next-year earnings estimate was revised up 1.4% in 30 days.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B from +10.6B, and net debt stands at 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while unpaid customer bills rose 61%.
Next-year earnings are estimated at 10.67 per share versus 12.8 this year, which lifts the forward P/E to 23.9, and operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 2–13%.

longterm.why: Today's rise took the price further above the 238.65 buy level, while the cash burn and slowing growth remain unresolved. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: At 255.39 the price is in the middle of its 251.93–258.08 zone, and resistance at 259.49–265.34 is within one typical day's move (the average true range, or typical daily move, is 10.38). The trend is a range with flat averages. No trade unless the price pulls back into 244.3–249.71 and holds, or closes above 265.34.

decision.timing: With no earnings date in the data, price levels set the timing. Options to 2026-12-18 price in a move of about 10.5% (priced off 246.82), and the largest open put positions sit at the 200 and 240 strikes.

change_mind: A filing showing 12-month free cash flow back above zero (it is -46.9B now), with operating margin holding at or above 13.09%, would turn the view to buy at 245.38.
Quarterly sales growth back above 16.61% would ease the slowdown concern; growth below 12.09% combined with operating margin back under 11.02% would move the view to avoid.
A close above 265.96 (top of the value range) would mean the price has left fair value, and the view would stay wait. A break below 233.59 would make 187.93 the next value reference.
